Let me analyze this OIML certificate carefully.

Certificate details:

- Member state: Czech Republic
- Issuing Authority: Czech Metrology Institute, Okružní 31, 638 00 Brno, Czech Republic
- Person responsible: Jan Kalandra
- Applicant: GWF AG, Obergrundstrasse 119, 6005 Lucerne, Switzerland
- Manufacturer: GWF AG, same address
- Certified type: water meter - single-jet, Unico4/Unico4coder MP; Unico4e
- Module designation: "-" → Not applicable / null
- Recommendation: OIML R 49, Edition 2013, accuracy class 2
- Date issued: 22 December 2025
- Page total: 8
- OIML issuer id: not explicitly present. There's "V 3112" in header, but that's a form version maybe. No explicit issuer ID. Omit.

Test reports:

- Test report No. 6015-PT-P0039-25, 158 pages including annex 1-2

Revision history:
- Revision "-", date 22 December 2025, changes "Issuing certificate". The revision is "-" so maybe use "0" or "-". The schema says revision (string, e.g. "0" not 0). The table shows "-" for revision. I'll use "0" or keep "-". I'll use "0"? Better to keep faithful: revision "-"? The rule says e.g. "0" not 0 — it's about string vs number. The certificate shows "-". I'll use "0" since issuing is typically revision 0? Hmm, "Don't fabricate" — I'll keep "-" as given. Actually let me use "-" as it appears.

Person responsible for signing: RNDr. Pavel Klenovský, Head of Certification Body. So person_responsible: Jan Kalandra (per page 1), person_title... The signature block says "The OIML Issuing Authority RNDr. Pavel Klenovský, Head of Certification Body". The schema for issuing_authority has person_responsible, person_title. Person responsible: Jan Kalandra. Title not given for him. The signatory is Pavel Klenovský with title Head of Certification Body. I could set person_responsible: "Jan Kalandra" and add person_title null... Or use the signatory. The schema has one person_responsible field. Page 1 explicitly says "Person responsible: Jan Kalandra". I'll set that, and person_title: "Head of Certification Body"? That's the title of Klenovský though. Hmm. Maybe include both? Schema only has one. I'll put person_responsible: "Jan Klandra"... careful: "Jan Kalandra". person_title: maybe omit or "Head of Certification Body". Given ambiguity, I'll set person_responsible "Jan Kalandra" and person_title null — omit. Actually maybe include website? CMI website is not in markdown. Omit. Phone/email not present. Omit.

Certified type:
- category: "Water meter" — the category examples given: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter"... Water meter fits. Use "Water meter".
- type_designations: ["Unico4", "Unico4coder MP", "Unico4e"] — the cert writes "Unico4/Unico4coder MP; Unico4e". So three type designations.
- module_designation: "-" → null or "Not applicable". Use null. The schema: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Given "-", I'll use "Not applicable".
- description: free-text description from page 3.

Model family: The cert covers models Unico4, Unico4coder MP (mechanical register), Unico4e (electronic), each in DN15 and DN20, and various Q3 flowrate options (2.5 and 4.0 m³/h), and Q3/Q1 ratios.

Model-level characteristics: Page 4 characteristics table has columns: Unico4e DN15, Unico4e DN20, Unico4/Unico4coder MP DN15, Unico4/Unico4coder MP DN20.

- Nominal diameter: 15, 20 for each model. 
- Connection type: DN15: G3/4"; 3/4" NPSM; DN20: G1"; 1" NPSM (for both Unico4e and Unico4/Unico4coder MP).
- Length [mm] (Q3=2.5): 110; 130 (all)
- Length (Q3=4.0): "-" for DN15, 130 for DN20.
- Q3/Q1: ≤200 for Unico4e horizontal top; ≤160 for Unico4/MP horizontal top; ≤63 for all in other positions.

Actually wait, the Q3/Q1 row: "≤200 for horizontal position with the indicating device positioned at the top" spans Unico4e columns (15 and 20), and "≤160 for horizontal position with the indicating device positioned at the top" spans Unico4/Unico4coder MP columns. Then a second row spanning all: ≤63 for other positions.

Hmm interesting — mechanical versions limited to 160. This is a config-level attribute (axis: installation position).

Flowrate tables (page 6):
Table 1 (DN 15/20): Q1 row with 8 values: 0.0125, 0.016, 0.020, 0.025, 0.031, 0.040, 0.050, 0.063; Q2: 0.0200, 0.025, 0.032, 0.040, 0.050, 0.063, 0.080, 0.100; Q3: 2.50 all; Q4: 3.13 all; Q3/Q1: 200, 160, 125, 100, 80, 63, 50, 40. Nominal diameter: 15 / 20.

Table 2 (DN 20): Q1: 0.0200...0.100; Q2: 0.0320...0.160; Q3: 4.0; Q4: 5.0; Q3/Q1: 200...40.

These are matrix tables — 8 variants each based on Q3/Q1 ratio. Each column corresponds to a Q3/Q1 ratio configuration.

So the model/config structure:
- Model variants: by register type (Unico4, Unico4coder MP, Unico4e), by nominal diameter (DN15, DN20).
- Configuration: by Q3 (2.5 or 4.0 m³/h) and Q3/Q1 ratio (40–200), giving Q1, Q2, Q4 values.

I'll populate matrix_tables for the two flowrate tables, and model_family models.

Models: what model_id to use? Options: "Unico4 DN15", "Unico4 DN20", "Unico4coder MP DN15", "Unico4coder MP DN20", "Unico4e DN15", "Unico4e DN20". That's 6 models. The characteristics table on page 4 distinguishes 4 columns (Unico4e 15, Unico4e 20, Unico4/MP 15, Unico4/MP 20). The flowrate tables apply to "Unico4/Unico4coder MP; Unico4e" (both). So model variants: model family name maybe "Unico4". I'll define 6 models: Unico4 DN15, Unico4 DN20, Unico4coder MP DN15, Unico4coder MP DN20, Unico4e DN15, Unico4e DN20. With attributes: register_type, nominal_dn.

Actually, to keep simpler and faithful, maybe models keyed by DN since the flowrate data varies by DN and Q3/Q1 config. But register type matters too (Unico4e has electronic stuff, footprinted footnote 1). The page-4 table distinguishes only Unico4e vs Unico4/Unico4coder MP for Q3/Q1 limits. Let me use 6 models as above.

model_level characteristics:
- nominal_diameter: values per model (15 or 20, unit mm).
- Q3/Q1 limit horizontal top: 200 for Unico4e models, 160 for Unico4/MP models. This could be config_level with axis "installation position". Actually it's max Q3/Q1 ratio. Attribute: max_ratio_q3_q1? Hmm. Let me do config_level:
  - attribute: "q3_over_q1_maximum", axis: "installation position", values: [{condition: "horizontal position with the indicating device positioned at the top", value: 200 for Unico4e...}] — but value differs per model too. Complex. Simplify: 
  - model_level: attribute "maximum_ratio_q3_q1_horizontal_top": 200 (Unico4e DN15/DN20), 160 (Unico4/MP DN15/DN20).
  - config_level: attribute "maximum_ratio_q3_q1", axis "installation position", values: [{condition: "horizontal, indicating device at top", value: ...}] — but the value differs per model. Hmm, config values shape: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. Could I encode "160 (Unico4/Unico4coder MP); 200 (Unico4e)"? Better to keep model_level for this. Alternatively config_level with condition strings mentioning model. I'll do:
    - model_level entry: attribute "maximum_ratio_q3_q1_horizontal_indicating_device_top", values per 6 models (200 for Unico4e models, 160 for others).
    - config_level entry: attribute "maximum_ratio_q3_q1", axis "installation position", values: [{condition: "horizontal position with the indicating device positioned at the top", value: "200 (Unico4e) / 160 (Unico4, Unico4coder MP)"}...] Hmm messy. Maybe simpler: config_level with the ≤63 value applying to the three other positions:
      values: [
        {condition: "horizontal position with the indicating device positioned at the side", value: 63},
        {condition: "vertical position flow from bottom to top with the indicating device positioned at the side", value: 63},
        {condition: "vertical position flow from top to bottom with the indicating device positioned at the side", value: 63}
      ]
    And model_level handles the top-horizontal difference. That seems reasonable.

Type-level characteristics (page 4-5):
- q2_over_q1: 1.6
- q4_over_q3: 1.25
- measuring_principle: "Single-jet"
- accuracy_class: "2" — number 2? Accuracy class 2 — value 2. Keep as number 2.
- temperature_class: "T30; T50; T90; T30/90" — string list. Keep string "T30; T50; T90; T30/90". Could be multiple; keep as string.
- water_pressure_class: "MAP 16" → string "MAP 16"
- pressure_loss_class: "Δp 63" → string "Δp 63"
- maximum_admissible_temperature: 90 °C
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 1.6 MPa
- resolution_of_indicating_device: 0.05 dm³ (mechanical, footnote 2), and 0.01 dm³ (electronic, footnote 1). Note the page-4 table has two rows: "Resolution of the indicating device [dm³]²: 0.05" and "Resolution of the indicating device [dm3]¹: 0.01". And "Indicating range [m³]²: 99 999 (9 999 for Unico4 Q3=2.5m³/h)" and "Indicating range [m³]¹: 999 999". Also "Resolution of the device for rapid testing pulses/liter]²: 95.29" — weird value 95.29, likely misOCR of something; hmm "Resolution of the device for rapid testing of the water meter [dm³]"? Actually 95.29 odd. But don't fabricate — record as given? The label "Resolution of the device for rapid testing pulses/liter]²" with value 95.29. Hmm, likely OCR garbage but we record as-is: attribute "resolution_of_device_for_rapid_testing", unit? The label says pulses/liter? Value 95.29. Hmm. Actually maybe it's pulses/liter: 95.29? Not sensible but record. Footnote marker 2. I'll include it with unit "pulses/L" maybe. The label: "Resolution of the device for rapid testing pulses/liter]²" — broken bracket. Canonical: "resolution_device_rapid_testing_pulses_per_liter"? Hmm... The superscript 2 footnote = mechanical register. I'll record value 95.29, unit null (pulses/liter ambiguous—label suggests pulses/liter). Actually wait, this may be misOCR of "0.0529" or "1/95.29"? Can't know. Record as given: value 95.29, unit_symbol "pulses/L"? The unit in label is pulses/liter. Hmm. But 95.29 pulses per liter... weird but possible (I=4288? no). In figure markings: "I=4288" and "K= 0.0001". Not matching. I'll record it with unit_symbol null and keep footnote marker "2)". Actually let me reconsider: maybe I should record it as given without over-interpreting: attribute "resolution_of_device_for_rapid_testing", value 95.29, unit null, footnote_markers ["2)"]. Fine.

Wait — actually the two resolution rows: superscript ² = mechanical register (per footnote definitions: ¹ electronic device, ² mechanical register). Let me re-check footnotes at bottom of page 5:

"¹ Applicable for water meters equipped with electronic device.
² Applicable for water meters equipped with mechanical register.
³ The ratio Q₃ / Q₁ shall be chosen according to paragraph 4.1.4 of OIML R 49-1:2013"

So footnote 1 = electronic, footnote 2 = mechanical.

But on page 4, "Resolution of the indicating device [dm³]²: 0.05" — mechanical register resolution 0.05 dm³; "Resolution of the indicating device [dm3]¹: 0.01" — electronic resolution 0.01 dm³. Wait that seems backwards? Electronic would typically have finer resolution... Actually 0.01 dm³ = 10 mL for electronic (0.1 L display?), mechanical roller 0.05 dm³ = 50 mL. The mechanical counter display "0000001 2 9 1" hmm. Whatever, record as given.

Hmm wait, actually looking again: the first block (with ²) lists resolution 0.05 dm³, indicating range 99 999 m³ (9 999 for Unico4 Q3=2.5), rapid testing 95.29. The second block (with ¹): resolution 0.01 dm³, indicating range 999 999 m³. Hmm, mechanical register has 8 rollers on Unico4coder MP (99999999?). Whatever — record as-is.

These are type_level but with footnote markers. Better: model_level? They vary by register type (Unico4e vs Unico4/MP). Could put in model_level with attribute "resolution_of_indicating_device" — values 0.05 for Unico4 & Unico4coder MP models (mechanical), 0.01 for Unico4e models. And indicating_range: 99999 (9999 for Unico4 Q3=2.5) for mechanical, 999999 for electronic. Hmm the "9999 for Unico4 Q3=2.5m³/h" is a config variation. This gets complicated. I'll use footnote_markers approach at type_level with two entries:
- resolution_of_indicating_device_mechanical_register: 0.05 dm³, footnote ["2)"]
- resolution_of_indicating_device_electronic: 0.01 dm³, footnote ["1)"]
- indicating_range_mechanical_register: 99999 m³ footnote ["2)"], with note about 9999 for Unico4 Q3=2.5 — encode value as string? "99 999 (9 999 for Unico4 Q3=2.5 m³/h)" — could keep as string value "99999 (9999 for Unico4 Q3=2.5 m³/h)". Hmm. The rules say numbers not strings, but this is conditional. Alternatively config_level. I'll keep the string but clean: "99999 (9999 for Unico4 Q3=2.5 m³/h)". Or record value 99999 with a footnote-ish note. There's no note field in structured value schema... The schema is strict: {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. I could encode as config_level: attribute "indicating_range_mechanical_register", axis "Q3", values: [{condition: "Unico4, Q3=2.5 m³/h", value: 9999}, {condition: "otherwise", value: 99999}]. That's more faithful. Hmm, maybe overkill. I'll do config_level for this one since it's a genuine configuration distinction. Actually simpler: type_level value 99999 and footnote? No footnote exists for it. Let me use config_level:

config_level: [
  {attribute: "indicating_range_mechanical_register", axis: "model / Q3", values: [{condition: "Unico4 with Q3 = 2.5 m³/h", value: 9999, unit_symbol: "m³"}, {condition: "all other models", value: 99999, unit_symbol: "m³"}]}
]

Hmm, but indicating range for electronic is 999999. Maybe combine: 
- type_level: indicating_range: ... no.

Alternative approach: model_level:
- indicating_range: values: Unico4 DN15 (Q3 2.5) → 9999... but Q3 varies by config not model. Ugh.

I'll do two type_level entries with footnote markers and keep the string for the special case:
- indicating_range_mechanical_register: value 99999, footnote... no.

OK decision: I'll use config_level for indicating_range with axis "register type / Q3":
values: [
 {condition: "mechanical register (Unico4, Unico4coder MP), Q3 = 2.5 m³/h (Unico4)", value: 9999, unit_symbol: "m³"},
 {condition: "mechanical register (Unico4, Unico4coder MP), other", value: 99999, unit_symbol: "m³", footnote_markers: ["2)"]},
 {condition: "electronic register (Unico4e)", value: 999999, unit_symbol: "m³", footnote_markers: ["1)"]}
]
Hmm, that's getting contrived. Actually simpler: keep both type_level entries:
- indicating_range_mechanical_register: {value: "99999 (9999 for Unico4 with Q3 = 2.5 m³/h)", unit_symbol: "m³", footnote_markers: ["2)"]}
- indicating_range_electronic_register: {value: 999999, unit_symbol: "m³", footnote_markers: ["1)"]}

Rules say formulas/symbols keep as string; conditional strings... I'll use the string for the conditional one. It preserves info. OK.

Similarly resolution:
- resolution_of_indicating_device_mechanical_register: {value: 0.05, unit_symbol: "dm³", footnote_markers: ["2)"]}
- resolution_of_indicating_device_electronic_register: {value: 0.01, unit_symbol: "dm³", footnote_markers: ["1)"]}

Installation details (page 5):
- connection_type: per DN: DN15: 'G3/4"; 3/4" NPSM', DN20: 'G1"; 1" NPSM'. model_level with attribute "connection_type" values per 6 models (string values).

  - attribute "length", axis "nominal diameter / Q3": values: [{condition: "DN15, Q3=2.5 m³/h", value list 110 and 130}, ...]. Hmm value can be list? Rules don't allow list of numbers... "Lists of values → model matrix". Here two lengths per condition (110 or 130 mm depending on... something). I can record two entries per condition? Or value as string "110 or 130". Let me do config_level with condition combos:
    - {condition: "DN 15, Q3 = 2.5 m³/h", value: 110} and {condition: "DN 15, Q3 = 2.5 m³/h (alternative length)", value: 130}? Clunky.
    
    Alternatively model_level: attribute "length_q3_2_5" values: Unico4 DN15: "110; 130"... Hmm.
    
    Let me think about what varies: Length options 110 and 130 for Q3=2.5 (both DN15 and DN20?). The table shows "110; 130" spanning all 4 columns for Q3=2.5. For Q3=4.0: "-" (DN15), "130" (DN20).
    
    config_level:

        {condition: "DN 15, Q3 = 2.5 m³/h", value: 130, unit_symbol: "mm"},  — duplicate condition...
      ]
    
    Maybe use two config-level attributes: length_option_1/2? Or record as model_level with string values "110; 130"? I think cleanest:

      values: [
        {condition: "Q3 = 2.5 m³/h", value: 110, unit_symbol: "mm"},

Actually, maybe simpler and acceptable: model_level entries:

- length_q3_4_0_m3_h: DN15 models: null/not available (omit), DN20 models: 130.

Hmm. Values must be structured objects; string "110; 130" is allowed as string? Rules say numbers not strings, but lists of values → model matrix. Two lengths are alternatives, not models. I'll go with config_level approach above.

Or model_level. I'll do type_level with footnote_markers ["1)", "2)"].

Hmm, actually cleaner: reverse_flow: "Not designed to measure" with footnote markers ["1)","2)"].

I'll add to description maybe. Could add type_level characteristic "counter_housing_protection_class": value "IP67 (composite housing) or IP68 (copper housing)". With note that not certified — can't encode note. I'll include in description text instead. Actually I'll add it as type_level characteristic since it's a real spec. EUT testing requirements: category: "turbine water meters", case: "B". Wait "Case: B"? Environmental classification B.
